defect_observations.observation: Proof of clause 4 of thm:p02-w02-p02-038-empty-comparison says 'The symbol set is at most countable (def:p02-many-sorted-signature); fix one injection of it into the natural numbers', and the body statement (parts file lines 600-604) says the clause 'uses no choice' for that reason. def:p02-many-sorted-signature (variants.tex 35-36) now lets Sort, F and R have any cardinality. So the cited premise is false as cited. Concrete case: countably many sorts (the variable form still applies) and uncountably many constants. The injection into N and the least-code choice of t_s are then unavailable, and the 'no choice' claim is unsupported. This is empty-sort (22.3) material, outside the strict reduction cited for D-P3-007.

thm:p02-many-sorted-translation (variants.tex 180) still declares proved=annex:p2.hol.5, but that annex text is a summary. It says 'Induction on terms, then on well-sorted formulas, gives ...' and 'The same induction gives truth preservation'. The written proof is clause 3 of thm:p02-w02-p02-038-strict-correspondence (038 annex 347-395, linked from 038 body 445-447) and the final paragraph of annex:p02-w02b-p02-033-variable-form (w02b annex 487-498). Coverage rests on those written proofs, not on the declared pointer.

The text asserts that the reduction transfers compactness and downward Lowenheim-Skolem, and that upward enlargement transfers when a specified sort is infinite. The extension-table row (variants.tex 460-468) repeats this, and 038 body 729-731 says the strict correspondence proves these transfers 'through it'. No derivation is written anywhere. The table row cites the variable-form theorem, which does not apply with uncountably many sorts. These claims are not among the owed D-P3-007 components.

tab:p02-w02-p02-038-conventions gives VarGuard_MS as the strict premise and does not mention the parameter form (ParGuard over L^n, w02b 303-321) needed for uncountably many sorts. The empty-sort and overlapping-sort reductions in this table rest on the variable injection. That limit is announced at 038 body 41-45 and w02b 490-493. With uncountably many sorts, no one-sorted reduction is given for either variant (22.3 scope).

The depth-gaps note for D-P3-007 reads 'only a second-order translation target at 10204'. In the held FLRV1 Version 1.0, lines 10203-10210 are the Foundation definition. The many-sorted second-order translation target is at lines 12582-12632 ('Worked many-sorted translation'). The note's substance is confirmed there: many-sorted logic appears only as that target, plus the nonempty-sort convention at 15196-15198 and a passing remark at 6057. The locator does not resolve in the held version. The handbook keeps the link to the second-order use (variants.tex 175-176; 038 body 732-733).

The existential case of the free-variable computation in thm:p02-w02b-p02-033-sentences is given as 'the same computation with \land in place of \to and \exists x_k in place of \forall x_k'. This is a 'similarly'-type step. It is not load-bearing: the restriction, tagging, reduction and variable-form proofs never use the sentencehood of translations.

The strict many-sorted signature does not require F and R to be disjoint. def:p02-many-sorted-translation (113-115) also does not say that s -> Q_s is injective. The flattened one-sorted signature needs both (inherited-03038-03104.tex requires F, R, Var and the logical tokens to be pairwise disjoint). The w02b convention at 58-62 asserts disjointness of F union R from the Q_s, Var and the logical tokens, but states neither of these two points.
